It reads the official API docs, studies every popular community CLI and MCP server, sniffs the web for the APIs nobody published (think Google Flights or Dominos), and applies the power-user playbook Peter Steinberger proved with discrawl and gogcli - local SQLite, compound commands, agent-native flags. It fuses all of that and prints a token-efficient Go CLI plus a Claude Code skill plus an MCP server for any API or any website.
Browse the full catalog of printed CLIs at printingpress.dev or in the Printing Press Library, organized by category, most with full MCP servers.
**Codex users:** see docs/CODEX.md to install the Printing Press skills with `--agent codex`, verify the install, and understand how that differs from `/printing-press <api> codex`.
**Cursor users:** see docs/CURSOR.md for how to install a printed CLI, attach the matching skill, handle auth, and choose CLI vs MCP when your repo does not already document a workflow.

**Prerequisites:** Go 1.26.10 or newer, Claude Code or another `skills`-supported agent, and Node/npm for `npx`. The skills are tested with Claude Code; install for Codex with `--agent codex` when you want to try the same slash-command workflow there. **Use Claude Code for the best-tested experience.**

Discord's API has 300+ endpoints. Most generators stop there - wrap every endpoint, ship it, done. But discrawl - Peter Steinberger's Discord tool - ignores most of them. It ships 11 commands: `sync`, `search`, `sql`, `tail`, `mentions`, `members`. 583 stars.

When choosing between Peter Steinberger's gogcli (6.5K+ stars, Go) and Google's official Workspace CLI (10K+ stars in a week, Rust), we ran /last30days - a recency research skill - across 34 X posts, 5 YouTube videos, and 10 web sources.

Full pipeline contract. The fast path above compresses a longer 9-phase managed pipeline: preflight, research, scaffold, enrich, regenerate, review, agent-readiness, comparative, ship. Inputs, outputs, gates, and artifacts for each phase are documented in docs/PIPELINE.md. Use it when you want to stop at any phase, resume later, re-run one step, or port the flow to another tool.
The generator ships three opt-in knobs on the spec's `mcp:` block, aligned with Anthropic's production-agent MCP guidance:
|Project Management|issue/task/ticket resources, assignee fields, priority levels|`stale`, `orphans`, `load`, `health`, `similar`|
Inspired by Peter Steinberger's gogcli. Two tiers, weighted 50/50. Grade A = 85+.
|Error Handling|Typed exits, retry with backoff, actionable error messages|
|+ 5 more|Terminal UX, README, Doctor, Local Cache, Breadth|
|Path Validity|Generated paths exist in the OpenAPI spec|
|Data Pipeline|Sync calls domain-specific UpsertX(), not generic Upsert()|
|Sync Correctness|Real resources, nested paths, pagination, incremental cursors|
|Type Fidelity|String IDs (not int), required params marked, quality descriptions|
|Dead Code|No unwired flags, no uncalled functions, no ghost tables|

**`/printing-press` slash command doesn't appear.** Restart or reload the agent session after installing the skills. For Claude Code, run `npx -y skills@latest list -g -a claude-code` to verify the install. For Codex, run `npx -y skills@latest list -g -a codex --json`. If you're developing from a clone in Claude Code, confirm `claude --plugin-dir .` was run from the cloned repo root or use the persistent local setup in Local Plugin Development.

If you use the clone-based developer path above, `claude --plugin-dir .` loads `/printing-press` from your working copy, so local skill edits take effect on the next session start. For a restart-safe local plugin setup, see Local Plugin Development. See AGENTS.md for full conventions, glossary, and release flow.
